d: An overview of audio features on Roblox.
h:
Adding audio to your games is crucial for elevating your games to new heights. By strategically using positional and non-positional audio, you can immerse players into your worlds, provide them useful feedback for their actions, and direct their attention to what they need to do to be successful in their objectives.

Audio assets

You can import audio assets that you're certain you have permission to use, such as audio that you make yourself. However, Roblox's Creator Store provides you a wide variety of free-to-use audio assets, including more than 100,000 professionally-produced sound effects and music tracks from top audio and music partners.

Audio objects

Roblox offers many different types of audio objects that you can use to play and modify your audio until it meets your game's design requirements:

  • The AudioPlayer object loads and plays the audio file using a set audio asset ID.
  • The AudioEmitter object is a virtual speaker that emits audio into the 3D environment.
  • The AudioListener object is a virtual microphone that picks up audio from the 3D environment.
  • The AudioDeviceOutput object is a physical hardware device within the real world, such as a speaker or headphones.
  • The AudioDeviceInput object is a physical microphone within the real world.
  • The AudioTextToSpeech object converts text to audio using an artificial voice.
  • The AudioSpeechToText object converts audio to text.
  • Wires carry audio streams from one object to another.

Using these objects, you can either set audio to play automatically at runtime, or trigger it to play from scripts. For practical applications of these audio objects, see the Add 2D audio, Add 3D audio, Add text-to-speech, Add speech-to-text, and Add voice chat tutorials.

Audio effects

Audio effects non-destructively modify or enhance audio streams from AudioPlayer objects. You can apply these effects to make your environments more captivating and immersive, such as using a AudioEqualizer object to make rain sound muffled, AudioCompressor object to control a sound's maximum volume, or AudioReverb to add more realistic reflections of sound in interior spaces.

kid.simple: This page is a quick tour of how sound works in Roblox games. Good sound makes your world feel real, tells players when they did something, and points them toward what to do next. You get sound files (called audio assets) from the Creator Store or by uploading your own. Then you use special audio objects to play those sounds, place them in the world, and change how they sound with effects.
kid.analogy: Think of setting up a band on a stage: you need the music (the audio file), a player to start it, speakers to send it out, cables to connect everything, and maybe some effect pedals to change the sound. Roblox audio objects are those same pieces, but virtual.
keyPoints: Sound helps players feel inside your world, gives feedback for their actions, and guides their attention.
Positional sound comes from a spot in the world; non-positional sound plays the same everywhere, like background music.
You can only upload audio you have permission to use, such as sounds you made yourself.
The Creator Store has more than 100,000 free sound effects and music tracks you can use.
`AudioPlayer` plays a sound file, `AudioEmitter` is a virtual speaker in the world, and `AudioListener` is a virtual microphone.
`AudioDeviceOutput` is the player's real speakers or headphones, and `AudioDeviceInput` is their real microphone.
`AudioTextToSpeech` turns text into a spoken voice, and `AudioSpeechToText` turns speech into text.
`Wire` objects carry sound from one audio object to the next, and audio effects like `AudioEqualizer`, `AudioCompressor`, and `AudioReverb` change how the sound comes out.

terms.audio asset: A sound file that lives on Roblox, like a song or a jump sound. Each one has an ID number you use to play it.
terms.asset ID: The unique number Roblox gives each uploaded file, so your game can point to it. For example, `rbxassetid://1234567`.
terms.positional audio: Sound that comes from a place in the 3D world. It gets louder as you walk toward it and quieter as you walk away.
terms.non-positional audio: Sound that plays at the same volume no matter where you stand, like menu music.
terms.Creator Store: Roblox's library of free things you can put in your game, including sounds and music.
terms.virtual speaker / virtual microphone: Pretend speakers and microphones that exist inside the game world instead of on your desk.
terms.audio stream: The flow of sound moving from one audio object to another, like water moving through a pipe.
terms.audio effect: An object that changes a sound on its way through, like making it echo or sound muffled.
terms.non-destructively: The effect changes what you hear, but the original sound file stays exactly the same. Remove the effect and the sound is back to normal.
terms.runtime: The time when the game is actually running and people are playing it, not when you are editing in Studio.

watchOut: Do not upload songs or sounds you found online unless you made them or have permission. Use the Creator Store for free, safe sounds.
An `AudioPlayer` alone makes no sound. It needs a `Wire` connecting it to something that outputs sound, like an `AudioDeviceOutput` or an `AudioEmitter`.
Older guides use the `Sound` object. The newer audio objects on this page can do more, so start with them for new projects.
